title: BJP holds Save Democracy rally in Lucknow

tea.why: The BJP organised rallies to oppose the INDIA bloc's narratives and to support the government's stance on electoral roll revisions.
tea.want: The party aims to counter opposition criticism and defend the government's democratic credentials.
tea.changed: Nov 3: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan led the march in Lucknow, criticising opposition leaders for allegedly destabilising the nation.

summary: On November 3, 2026, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) held a 'Save Democracy' rally in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan led the march, which party members described as a 'Satyagraha against anarchy'. Participants carried flags and posters to express support for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and to criticise the Congress party and the INDIA bloc. The organisers accused opposition leaders of attempting to destabilise democratic institutions and politicising the ongoing electoral roll revision (SIR) process. Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan specifically targeted Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh Yadav during his address. Similar rallies were held in Bareilly on the same day, led by other senior BJP figures including JP Nadda and Jayant Chaudhary. No official response from the opposition or authorities regarding the protest's impact was reported.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

crowd.text: More than 50,000 party workers and supporters took to the streets in Lucknow and Bareilly according to Bhaskar English.

updates.text: BJP supporters held a 'Save Democracy' rally in Lucknow, led by Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan.
